$comment: The deployment register: what was deployed, where, from which commit, and who recorded it.
It exists because a production system disappeared and this repository could not say which one it
was. An App Platform app ran in blr1 from 2026-10-05 — commit a468403 sized it, c209a3e created the
first CMS account and f1f7e97 the first staff credential, so it was live and migrated — and five
weeks later the account held no app and no managed database. Nothing here recorded its id, its URL
or the commit it served, because `.do/README.md` is written with `<app-id>` placeholders and no step
ever captured the real one. So the questions 'which app was it', 'when did it go' and 'what was
running' have no answer in the repository, and the DigitalOcean API does not list deleted apps.
That is the same failure this build spends most of its gates refusing: `artifacts/drills` records a
restore, `artifacts/release/freeze.json` records a freeze, `pnpm go-no-go` refuses on an absent fact
with 'we did not measure it and it failed have the same consequence' — and the deployment itself,
the one thing customers touch, was the fact nobody measured.
It ships LIVE AND OPEN rather than absent, which is freeze.json's and ADR 0125's argument: a
register created on the day somebody needs it is a register nobody has read, and a missing one is
indistinguishable from an estate nobody deployed.
NOTHING WRITES HERE AUTOMATICALLY. `pnpm deployment:record` appends an entry from facts a person
supplies, validates every one of them, and invents none — the same shape as the freeze register,
and for the same reason: a mechanism that guessed the live URL would be recording a claim this
build made up (brief rule 15). `pnpm deployment:verify` refuses a malformed register, an entry
naming a commit that is not in this history, and an entry that claims to supersede one it predates.
`retired` is set when a deployment is taken down, with the instant and the reason, and the entry is
never deleted. The whole value of this file is that it still holds the row for a thing that no
longer exists.
